entry.title: Café Meherban
entry.hook: One month. ₹600. One table. Let's see where it goes.
entry.boss: A boss fight where the boss is the month. Nobody gets hurt.
entry.objective: By the end you can put money aside first, spot small spends, keep a cushion, and know what borrowing really costs.
entry.note: All amounts are made up, for practice.
entry.privacy: We save only your game choices, not who you are.

hud.fictional: Quick Cash is a made-up example, not a real company.
hud.ledgerEmpty: Nothing yet. Chacha is sharpening his pencil.

src.question: Where should this ₹{{x}} come from?
src.emergency: This is your cushion. Something may be coming.

goals.reactEarphones: Earphones. Good. The bus is long.
goals.reactTrip: A trip. Those stories last longer than the chai.
goals.reactController: A controller. Your thumbs will thank you.

r0.l1: First of the month. You walk in like everyone does.
r0.l3: An envelope lands on the table. ₹600 in notes, and a note.
r0.note: Chacha knows how to count. Listen. Then decide. Ammamma
r0.l4: Her handwriting has not changed in forty years.
r0.l5: ₹600. One month. Let's see where it goes.
r0.l6: Four hard parts and a cloud. I will be here. Polishing.
r0.l7: Every customer wants something. What is pinned on my board for you?
r0.l8: ₹250 on the board. That is the target. Everything else is life.
r0.l9: One guess before we start. No marks. I just like to know what people think.
r0.predict: How many surprises do you think this month will send you?
r0.none: None. It will be a calm month.
r0.rNone: A calm month. Lovely. I will write it down.
r0.rOne: One. I will write that down too.
r0.rTwo: Two or more. You are an optimist about problems.
r0.rIdk: Honest. The best answer in this café.

r1.l1: Money on the first always gets spent. The only question is who decides where.
r1.l2: Three places. The tumbler is for spending.
r1.l3: The gullak is for your goal. It sits high on my shelf. Seen, not reached.
r1.l4: The umbrella stand, by the door. For rain.
r1.l5: That cloud? It has been there since you walked in. I do not know what it carries.
r1.l6: Three small bills are coming this month. They do not wait for a good moment.
r1.hint: Drag the coins, or use the + buttons. Nothing starts until every coin has a home.
r1.saveZero: Nothing on the shelf. We will see what finds it.
r1.saveFull: The whole goal, already on the shelf. Now you live on what is left.
r1.spendBig: Most of it in the tumbler. We will see how long a tumbler lasts.
r1.emergencySmall: A little by the door. A little is a start.
r1.emergencyBig: Something by the door. The cloud will be curious.
r1.balanced: A bit of everything. Let us see if it holds.
r1.allSave: All on the shelf. Impressive. And how are you getting to class?
r1.mind: The month is long. Mind the window.

bill.chachaAuto: Bills do not ask. They arrive.
bill.chachaData: Data does not run on hope.
bill.chachaLunch: Exams are a month's worth of hungry in one afternoon.
bill.fromSave: Off the shelf, for a bill. The goal moves back.

window.hint: Tap Let it cool. Chai cools in the saucer. So do wants. Sometimes.
window.short: The tumbler is short. The gullak is not.
window.dynRow: In a row. The tumbler sounds different now.
window.dynDrop: Two cooled and gone. The tumbler thanks you.
window.dynNone: Nothing at all? The vendors will talk about you.
window.dynBusy: A busy window. I will need a bigger page.
window.fizzing: The orange bottle is fizzing. I will say no more.
window.summary: You looked at {{n}} things. You got {{g}}. You let {{m}} cool. Tumbler: ₹{{x}}.
window.bottles: The orange bottle is {{fun}}. The teal one is {{friends}}.

gamepack.name: Game pack
gamepack.pitch: New season pack! ₹50! Your friends already have it!
gamepack.get: A game pack. Played twice by Friday, I would guess.
gamepack.coolYes: Wanted it after the wait. Good sign.
gamepack.coolNo: The pack will be there tomorrow. They always are.

jacket.name: Jacket
jacket.pitch: SALE ENDS TODAY! ₹200 only! Last one!
jacket.get: A jacket. In Hyderabad. In October.
jacket.coolYes: Still wanted after the chai cooled. Fair.
jacket.coolNo: The banner says today. He was here yesterday, too.
jacket.pass: The banner man will try again tomorrow.

match.name: Match ticket
match.get: A match ticket. I hope the seat is good.
match.soldOut: Sold out. Sometimes things really do run out. Waiting is a check, not a rule.
match.soldOutNo: It sold out. You did not mind.

cover.name: Phone cover
cover.get: A cover. Your phone may thank you.
cover.coolNo: Skipped the cover. Phones are tough. Mostly.

coins.name: In-game coins
coins.line: Coins pack, ₹30, for the next level.

trolley.l1: Yusuf comes by every day. Never pushy. That is how it works.
trolley.noSaucer: No saucer here. Nobody puts a ₹10 biscuit in a saucer.
trolley.streakOk: Yusuf is smiling. He has a gift.
trolley.end: That is the trolley. Now, close your eyes.
trolley.predict: Without the ledger: how much did the little things cost you?
trolley.above: You guessed {{range}}. The plates say ₹{{x}}. Little things have long bills.
trolley.inside: You guessed {{range}}. The plates say ₹{{x}}. You were paying attention. Keep doing that.
trolley.below: You guessed {{range}}. Only ₹{{x}}. You were more careful than you thought.
trolley.nothing: Not a single biscuit? Yusuf is worried. Still, ₹0 is a number worth knowing.
trolley.worth1: Spending is fine. Spending without noticing is the problem. So, notice.
trolley.worthPrompt: Tag each one. Only you know.
trolley.worthMeh: The meh pile is the interesting one. ₹{{y}}. That is how far your goal could have moved.
trolley.worthAllGlad: All glad. That is a good month's spending, whatever the total.
trolley.worthNone: Nothing bought, nothing to tag. Noted.

bn.title: Big Night
bn.refused2: There goes the marble. {{a}}. {{b}}. Small noes, one after another.
bn.refused1: There goes the marble. {{a}}. One no after another.
bn.inviteFun: Big screen on the terrace tonight, the cricket final. ₹{{x}} each. Everyone is going. Last chance?
bn.inviteFriends: Ayesha's birthday dinner, ₹{{x}} each. Everyone is going. Last chance?
bn.chacha: A small yes now saves a large one later. Or it does not. You know your own month.
bn.hint: Pick what you can live with. Nobody keeps score.
bn.goSub: From any jar you choose. The bottle resets.
bn.halfSub: From any jar you choose. The bottle drops to half.
bn.staySub: No cost. The bottle stays full and comes with you into next month, bigger.
bn.rHalf: Half and home early. Sensible, or sad. Only you know.
bn.rStay: Stayed in. The money stayed. So did the fizz.
bn.carried: You stayed in last month. The bottle remembered. It is bigger this time.

teja.l1: Hey! You will not believe it. Saturday's match, student stand, ₹100 a ticket. And I am ₹100 short.
teja.l1kit: Hey! My project kit is due Monday. ₹100. And I am ₹100 short.
teja.l2: Can you lend me ₹100? I will give it back Friday. Promise.
teja.aside: Friday is a very popular day in this café.
teja.rule: I lend only what I can afford to forget. You should, too.
teja.hint: Choose what you can afford to wait on.
teja.sub_lend100: Out of Spend: ₹100. Back: Teja says Friday.
teja.sub_lend50: Out of Spend: ₹50. Back: Teja says Friday.
teja.sub_gift30: Out of Spend: ₹30. Not expected back.
teja.sub_no: No change. Teja hears: 'I cannot this month. Next chai is on me.'
teja.you_gift30: Here, ₹30. Do not worry about it.
teja.you_no: I cannot this month. Next chai is on me.
teja.t_lend100: You are the best! Friday, I swear.
teja.t_lend50: ₹50 is perfect. That covers most of it. Thank you!
teja.t_gift30: You do not have to! ...Okay, thank you. I owe you a chai.
teja.t_no: Deal! Next chai is yours, then.
teja.c_lend100: ₹100 leaves the tumbler. It is with Teja now. Until Friday, it is not yours to use.
teja.c_lend50: 'I can do ₹50.' Five words. Very useful.
teja.c_gift30: A gift is simple. Nobody has to remember anything on Friday.
teja.c_no: A good friend survives a 'no'. Especially a kind one.
teja.honest: Honest. Money you do not have cannot be lent.

rain.calm: Quiet. The fans turn. Chacha polishes the same glass.
rain.crack: The phone slides off the marble. Crack.
rain.first1: There. That is what the cloud was carrying.
rain.first2: Tyres. They always choose a rainy day.
rain.first3: The office never mentions it until the last week.
rain.first4: Weddings arrive on schedule. The money does not.
rain.first5: Some surprises are not optional. That is what the door is for.
rain.letter: It does not send a letter first. It just rains.
rain.bill2: Bicycle puncture and a new tyre
rain.bill4: Cousin's wedding gift plus auto fares
rain.bill5: Doctor's visit and medicines for Ammamma
rain.cover: The cover took half the fall.
rain.tSave: On the shelf: ₹{{x}}. The goal says ₹250.
rain.tPlates: The little things: ₹{{x}}. They are still on the table.
rain.tTeja: ₹{{x}} is with Teja. Teja is at the match.
rain.payLine: Pay it from wherever you like. Every source has a price. Look at them.
rain.hint: Move coins into the bill until it is covered.
rain.qcPitch: Cracked screen? No stress! Get ₹{{x}} in 30 seconds! No documents!
rain.qcAsk: Before you flip it: if you borrow ₹150, how much do you pay back?
rain.flipNote1: You pay this on payday, whether or not you are ready.
rain.flipNote2: If you cannot pay it all, the rest is still owed.
rain.noFlip: You did not flip it. Everything has a back.
rain.gLow: You guessed ₹{{g}}. The card says ₹{{r}}. ₹{{d}} for the speed.
rain.gEq: You guessed it. Read the back, always.
rain.gHigh: You guessed ₹{{g}}. It is ₹{{r}}. You expected the worst, and it was close.
rain.oEmergency: The umbrella stand has earned its place.
rain.oBetween: Between the door and the tumbler. The shelf survives.
rain.oSave: Off the shelf it comes. The goal paid for the rain.
rain.oQuick: Done in 30 seconds. ₹{{r}} on payday. The extra ₹{{e}} is the price of the speed.
rain.oMore: More by the door than the rain needed. The rest stays for next month.

tally.settleNone: Nothing owed. Cleanest page in the book.
tally.settleQuick: Payday. Quick Cash collects ₹{{r}}. The extra ₹{{e}} goes with it.
tally.settleOwed: ₹{{o}} still owed. It comes out of next month's money before you see it.
tally.clock: The clock never moves. Your month did.
tally.reached: Goal reached. Here is how you did it.
tally.reachedCost: Goal reached. The loan cost you ₹{{e}} on the way.
tally.notyet: Not this month. Want to see what moved?
tally.secReachedSpent: You spent ₹{{w}} on things you valued and still got there. That is the whole trick.
tally.secReachedNone: You got there by saying no to everything. Look at the bottle. That is what it cost.
tally.secShortSpent: You spent on things you valued. The goal needed ₹{{x}} more. Both are true.
tally.secShortNone: Nothing on wants, and the month still got to you. Look at where the bills came from.
tally.kind: What kind of money manager were you this month?
tally.close: Same table. New month. Change one thing and we go again.
tally.nobody: Nobody here was born knowing this.

fastmover.name: The Fast Mover
fastmover.line: You moved fast when it mattered. Speed has a price, and you paid it with your eyes open.

openhand.name: The Open Hand
openhand.line: You looked after a friend first. I have seen worse plans. I have seen better timing.

windowwaiter.name: The Window Waiter
windowwaiter.line: You let things cool. Some you kept, some you dropped. The pause is yours now.

quietholder.name: The Quiet Holder
quietholder.line: You said no all month. It worked, and the bottle is still fizzing. Both are true.

shelffirst.name: The Shelf First
shelffirst.line: You paid the shelf first and lived on what was left. The month had to fit around it.

doorwatcher.name: The Door Watcher
doorwatcher.line: You kept something by the door. The rain came, and the door held.

evenkeeper.name: The Even Keeper
evenkeeper.line: A bit of everything. Not a pattern yet. That is fine. Patterns come with the second month.

note.billFromSave: Off the shelf, for a bill.

cb.flip: You borrowed without flipping the card. I would flip it next time.
cb.teja: Teja had your ₹{{l}} when the rain came. I mention it only because I am watching.
cb.stayed: You said no to the night. The bottle did not forget.
cb.brave: At the start I said 'brave'. It was an accurate word.
cb.saidNone: You said none. The cloud said one.
cb.yusuf: You guessed low. It was ₹{{x}}. Yusuf is a patient man.
cb.walkedAway: You let it cool and walked away from ₹{{x}}. I notice these things.
cb.marble: You spent ₹{{x}} early on what you wanted. The marble never popped.
cb.saidOne: You said one. Right. Expecting it is its own skill.
cb.saidIdk: You said no idea. The honest answer. Now you have an idea.

quick.a: You borrowed ₹{{b}} and paid back ₹{{r}}: ₹{{e}} extra, about {{pct}} percent, within days.
quick.b: Fast money has its price on the back. A cushion would have cost nothing extra.
quick.c: Before borrowing, read what you pay back, not what you get.

covered.a: The umbrella stand covered ₹{{c}} of the ₹{{b}} bill.
covered.b: A cushion turns a surprise into an inconvenience instead of a debt.
covered.c: Start a cushion with even ₹20 a month. Aim first for one small surprise.

notCovered.a: The ₹{{b}} bill came from your other jars.
notCovered.b: Without a cushion, a surprise is paid for by your goal, a loan, or both.
notCovered.c: Next payday, set something aside before spending. Even ₹50 helps.

went.a: A want kept building until the Big Night, and you went.
went.b: A want that is refused again and again can grow into one big spend. Small, planned yeses can be cheaper.
went.c: Pick one want you keep refusing. Decide a small amount for it each month.

stayed.a: You stayed in, and the money stayed. The bottle is still full.
stayed.b: Refusing is allowed. It can build pressure, and it helps to notice it instead of pretending it is not there.
stayed.c: Say out loud one thing you are skipping, and when you might say yes.

none.a: Your bills came to ₹80 and your wants to ₹{{w}}.
none.b: Bills are not choices. Wants are. Telling them apart is the first move in any budget.
none.c: Write next month's bills first. What is left is yours to plan.

low.a: The little things came to ₹{{x}}, above your guess.
low.b: Small amounts feel too small to count, so they skip the checks we use on big ones.
low.c: Pick one small daily spend. Add up its cost for a month.

ok.a: You kept the little things to ₹{{x}}.
ok.b: Noticing is what keeps small spends small.
ok.c: Look at one regular small spend and ask: am I glad about this one?

dropped.a: You let {{m}} things cool. {{d}} lost their shine, saving ₹{{x}}.
dropped.b: A pause separates 'I want it now' from 'I want it'.
dropped.c: Wait a night before buying anything unplanned over ₹100.

still.a: You let {{m}} cool and still bought {{y}}.
still.b: That is a decision, not an impulse. Waiting is a check, not a rule.
still.c: Keep using the pause. You will learn your wants.

never.a: You decided on the spot every time.
never.b: Sellers say 'today only' because pauses work against them.
never.c: Pick one item to put off for a night and see what happens.

lent.a: ₹{{l}} was with Teja when the rain came.
lent.b: Lent money is not yours to use until it returns, and friends are sometimes slower than Friday.
lent.c: Lend only what you could live without for a while, and say the amount out loud.

gift.b: A small gift keeps things simple. Nobody has to remember anything.
gift.c: If you cannot wait for it back, give less and do not expect it.

no.b: A kind no protects the friendship and the plan.
no.c: Keep one sentence ready: 'I cannot this month. Next chai is on me.'

reached.a: You reached ₹250, spent ₹{{x}} on wants and little things, and kept ₹{{y}} for rain.
reached.b: Every rupee has many possible uses. A goal helps you choose which one wins.
reached.c: Name your next goal and give it a date.

short.b: Goals move when other things claim the money. Seeing which ones is the first step.
short.c: Pick the biggest mover and decide in advance how much of it you will allow.

big.a: You put ₹{{s}} in the gullak before the first chai.
big.b: Money set aside first is protected from the small things that show up later.
big.c: On the day money arrives, move a fixed amount to a separate place before you spend any.

small.b: What you set aside first is what you keep. What you leave for later has many claims on it.
small.c: Decide the amount before the money arrives, even if it is small.

chit.quick: This week: find out what it would cost to keep ₹150 by the door. Start with ₹20.
chit.emergency: This week: put even ₹20 somewhere you will not touch.
chit.stayed: This week: name one thing you are skipping, and one you will say yes to.
chit.little: This week: write down every spend under ₹50 for three days.
chit.cool: This week: wait one night before one unplanned purchase.
chit.lend: This week: practise one sentence: 'I can do ₹50.'
chit.goal: This week: write down your next goal and a date next to it.

replay.title: One change
replay.ask: Same table. New month. Pick one thing to do differently.
replay.little: Skip more of the little things
replay.react: One change. Good. That is how people learn here. One thing at a time.
replay.back: Back again. Good. The chai is still warm.
replay.flipped: Behaviours that showed up this month: {{n}}
replay.eDoor: More by the door this time. Look at how the rain was paid.
replay.eShelf: You chose the shelf. The gullak says ₹{{x}} now.
replay.eCool: You chose to let things cool. {{d}} lost their shine this month.
replay.eLittle: You chose the little things. They came to ₹{{x}}, last time ₹{{y}}.
replay.eTeja: You chose Teja. This time you lent ₹{{x}}.
replay.eFine: You chose the fine print. Borrowing is easier to judge once you have read the back.
replay.eYes: You chose to say yes on purpose. Look at the bottle this time.
replay.eSurprise: No plan, no pattern. Let us see what you do next month.
replay.tejaEpilogue1: Teja said Friday. The game ends before Friday.
replay.tejaEpilogue2: Friday came. Teja paid back ₹{{x}}, with a chai.
